cluster_summary: Shell command injection vulnerabilities caused by inadequate handling of shell metacharacters in either command construction or input validation. One sub-pattern involves insufficient escaping when building shell arguments, allowing metacharacters to break quoting. Another covers allowlist-based validators that miss certain shell constructs, enabling bypass. A third includes missing or easily bypassed input validation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Extend the parser to detect and reject these constructs before allowlist matching, including platform-specific checks and handling of backslash-newline continuations..

sub_patterns.name: Incomplete shell command allowlist validation
sub_patterns.root_cause: Allowlist-based command parsers fail to detect certain shell constructs such as platform-specific metacharacters (Windows &), line continuations, command substitution inside double quotes, and parameter expansions in heredocs, allowing attackers to inject arbitrary commands.
